claims.excerpt: How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Water
claims.claim: GRACE Follow-On tracks changes in Earth’s water.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The mission follows changes involving groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, ice sheets and changes in sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.narrative: Explain how GRACE Follow-On’s two satellites use changes in the distance between them to help investigate water movement on Earth.
claims.explanation: “Tracks” summarizes the source’s description of following water-related changes; it does not claim direct observation of water.
claims.materiality: The headline accurately summarizes the mission’s described subject.

claims.excerpt: GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart.
claims.claim: GRACE Follow-On has two satellites following one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: Twin satellites follow each other about 137 miles or 220 kilometers apart.
claims.narrative: GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart.
claims.explanation: The satellite count and approximate separation match the source.

claims.excerpt: As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite.
claims.claim: As the satellites approach a larger mass concentration, gravity affects the leading satellite before the trailing one and initially pulls the leading satellite farther away.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, stronger gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing one.
claims.narrative: As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite.
claims.explanation: The sequence and direction of the initial separation change match the source. Omitting “stronger” does not change the stated relationship in this context.
claims.materiality: Accurately describes the physical effect central to the explanation.

claims.excerpt: The changing distance between the satellites is a measurement scientists use to infer shifts in mass.
claims.claim: Scientists use changes in the distance between the satellites as a measurement to infer shifts in mass.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The changing inter-satellite distance is a raw measurement used to infer shifts in mass.
claims.narrative: That changing separation is a measurement used to infer shifts in mass
claims.explanation: The piece accurately describes the changing separation as a measurement used to infer mass shifts.
claims.materiality: Preserves the distinction between the measured quantity and the inferred quantity.

claims.excerpt: It is not a direct measurement of groundwater;
claims.claim: The satellite separation measurement does not directly measure groundwater.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The changing inter-satellite distance is a raw measurement used to infer shifts in mass.
claims.narrative: Do not describe the separation measurement as a change in altitude or as a direct image or measurement of groundwater.
claims.explanation: The source describes distance as a measurement used to infer mass shifts, not as a direct groundwater measurement.
claims.materiality: This distinction prevents readers from mistaking an indirect inference for direct groundwater measurement.

claims.excerpt: the inferred mass changes can help reveal water movement on Earth.
claims.claim: Inferred mass changes can help reveal water movement on Earth.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The changing inter-satellite distance is a raw measurement used to infer shifts in mass. The mission follows changes involving groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, ice sheets and changes in sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.narrative: That changing separation is a measurement used to infer shifts in mass, which can reveal changes involving groundwater and other stores of water.
claims.explanation: The source connects inferred mass shifts with the mission’s tracking of water-related changes; “can help reveal” appropriately expresses an indirect, qualified relationship.
claims.materiality: Accurately conveys the purpose of the inference without claiming direct measurement of water.

claims.excerpt: These changes include shifts in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, as well as sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.claim: The water-related changes include groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, ice sheets, and sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The mission follows changes involving groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers, ice sheets and changes in sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.narrative: including changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
claims.explanation: The listed water stores and the qualification limiting the sea-level changes to water added to the oceans match the source.
claims.materiality: The qualification is material because it avoids extending the claim to other causes of sea-level change.
